methods.label: Determine the linear remainder
methods.explanation:
The divisor \((x-19)(x-99)\) has degree 2, so its remainder has the form \(mx+n\), including the possibility of a constant remainder. Thus, for some polynomial \(Q(x)\),
\[
P(x)=(x-19)(x-99)Q(x)+mx+n.
\]
The given linear-divisor remainders tell us that \(P(19)=99\) and \(P(99)=19\). Substituting these inputs makes the product term vanish, giving
\[
19m+n=99,\qquad 99m+n=19.
\]
Subtracting the first equation from the second eliminates \(n\):
\[
80m=-80,\qquad m=-1.
\]
Then \(-19+n=99\), so \(n=118\). Therefore the remainder is \(\boxed{-x+118}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
